full_judgment: 10. Mr Khair Ezaz Masod, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite party submits that although no specific issue was framed in the earlier Title Suit No. 69 of 1993 in respect of adoption of plaintiff but impliedly that issue was dealt with in the suit, which have been materially and substantially decided, same cannot again be the subject matter of issue in the present suit to be adjudicated upon. He further submits that the father of the plaintiff, Khitish did not file any appeal against the finding `Dattak' passed in previous Title Suit No.69 of 1993, although he was fully aware about "Dattak". In this connection, the learned Advocate refers two decision reported in AIR 1924 (PC) 144 and AIR 1932 (PC) 50. He next submits that the learned Advocate for the petitioner failed to show any misreading, misconstruction and non-consideration of any facts and evidence which was concurrently found by the courts below. The appellate court rightly affirmed the judgment and decree of trial court by holding that the plaintiff was adopted by the adoptive father Khitish Chandra Saha after complying the provision of Hindu law and completing the ceremony called "datta homam" for adoption as required under the Hindu law. In this respect learned Advocate refers Article 489 of Mulla Principles of Hindu Law, Sixteenth Edition, page 516 and accordingly prayed for discharge of the Rule.
